panels.title: Throughput (req/s)
panels.description: Requests answered by the MaaS Gateway for this namespace (istio_requests_total), all response codes.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Share of non-2xx responses returned to clients by the MaaS Gateway (istio_requests_total).

panels.title: Latency breakdown per request (mean)
panels.description: Mean seconds per request spent waiting for a slot (queue), processing the prompt (prefill) and generating tokens (decode). The tallest band is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Share of request time
panels.description: Each stage's mean divided by queue+prefill+decode: which stage dominates each request (legend = true shares).

panels.title: TTFT p95 by priority (EPP)
panels.description: EPP-measured TTFT per InferenceObjective priority. Inversion: p100 at or above p0.

panels.title: EPP queue wait by priority (mean)
panels.description: Time spent in the EPP Flow Control queue. Flow Control must be enabled. Inversion: p100 wait > p0 wait.

panels.title: Where requests wait: EPP priority queue vs vLLM FCFS queue
panels.description: Priority only applies while requests wait in the EPP queue. A queue building inside vLLM (utilization-detector) is FCFS and causes priority inversion.

panels.title: Dispatched req/s by priority and pool saturation
panels.description: Request throughput per priority; saturation (right axis) is the detector output (>=1 means saturated).

panels.title: Requests/s by pod
panels.description: How EPP splits requests across vLLM pods. no-hit-lru / kv-cache-utilization scorers change this split.

panels.title: Prefix cache hit rate by pod
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens served from the prefix cache. prefix-cache-scorer raises this by routing a document back to the pod that cached it.

panels.title: KV cache usage by pod
panels.description: KV cache in use per pod. kv-cache-utilization-scorer steers new requests away from the fuller pod.

panels.title: TTFT p50 / p95
panels.description: End effect of routing: cache hits shorten prefill and therefore TTFT.

panels.title: Replicas: desired / updated / available
panels.description: Zero-downtime rollout: 'available' never drops below 'desired' while 'updated' climbs to it.

panels.title: Pod ready (vLLM workload)
panels.description: Ready = model loaded and /health OK. New pods turn Ready before old ones leave.

panels.title: Throughput by pod
panels.description: Requests completed by each vLLM pod. Traffic moves from old to new pods during a rollout.

panels.title: Error rate by pod (vLLM, reference only)
panels.description: Only requests a pod actually processed and ended with error/abort. Rollout failures (sent to a loading or terminated pod, cut connections) never reach vLLM metrics -> judge with the Gateway panels.

panels.title: Gateway responses by HTTP code
panels.description: What clients actually received from the MaaS Gateway. Anything other than 200 during a rollout is a lost request.

panels.title: Pod startup time (start -> Ready)
panels.description: Per pod: model download (storage-initializer) + model loading + vLLM init. Grows with model size.

targets.expr: label_replace(max by (pod)(kube_pod_status_ready_time{namespace="$namespace", pod=~".+-kserve-[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]{5}"}) - max by (pod)(kube_pod_start_time{namespace="$namespace", pod=~".+-kserve-[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]{5}"}), "short", "$1", "pod", ".*-([a-z0-9]+)$")

panels.title: Gateway failures by cause (non-2xx)
panels.description: Client-visible failures split by Envoy response flag. UF = connect to pod failed, UC = connection cut mid-request, UH/NR = no pod to route to, URX = retries exhausted, '-' = error returned by the pod or auth. Flat 0 during a rollout = zero downtime.

panels.title: Multimodal cache hit rate by pod
panels.description: Share of image inputs whose encoder output was reused (vLLM mm cache). EPP sends a re-requested image to the pod that already encoded it.

panels.title: Prefix cache hit rate by pod
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens (image tokens included) served from the prefix cache.

panels.title: Prompt tokens per request: total vs computed
panels.description: The gap between the two lines is what the prefix cache saved. Image tokens are ~1,000 per image.

panels.title: Prefill time per request (mean)
panels.description: Time to process the prompt (image + text). Cache hits skip most of it.

panels.title: TTFT p50 / p95
panels.description: End effect of multimodal-aware routing.

panels.title: Requests/s by pod
panels.description: Load split across VLM pods.

panels.title: Requests/s by pod
panels.description: Cache-first (P1) sends a hot document to one pod; load-first (P2) splits it once a queue forms.

panels.title: Queued requests by pod (load signal)
panels.description: vLLM queue per pod. queue/kv scorers only differentiate pods when this is above zero.

panels.title: Running requests by pod
panels.description: Requests executing per pod (capped by --max-num-seqs). One pod at the cap and the other idle = skewed routing.

panels.title: Prefix cache hit rate by pod
panels.description: What cache-first buys: document reuse per pod.

panels.title: TTFT p50 / p95
panels.description: End effect of the policy on latency.

panels.title: Queue time per request (mean)
panels.description: Time spent waiting in vLLM. Grows when a policy piles requests onto one pod.

panels.title: EPP plugin latency p95 by plugin
panels.description: Time each EPP plugin adds per request. token-producer = round trip to the external tokenizer.

panels.title: EPP scheduling latency p50 / p95
panels.description: End-to-end time the EPP takes to pick a pod.

panels.title: CPU: tokenizer vs EPP
panels.description: Tokenization load moves from the EPP to the separate tokenizer Deployment.

panels.title: Memory: tokenizer vs EPP
panels.description: Working set of the tokenizer (loads the model tokenizer) and the EPP.

panels.title: Prefix cache hit rate
panels.description: Cache-aware routing quality with external vs built-in tokenization.

targets.legendFormat: prefix cache hit rate - all pods

panels.title: TTFT p50 / p95
panels.description: End effect on latency.
